assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Removing the fleet-record read, or returning a constant node, reddens this arm: the decision would hold instead of releasing. The source run's negative-control.log records exactly that mutation and this arm failing.

Releasing unconditionally, or reading the unit name from anywhere but the environment, reddens the release/no-unit split: the foreign-host arm at lines 119-130 asserts release-and-exit with unit_disable_command None when the unit env is unset.

A decision that releases without checking either the same-host arm or the no-run-on-node arm reddens these hold arms; they pass in the recorded negative control because that mutation pushes toward hold.

A decision that writes the real fleet record or claims the real seat reddens this arm; the before/after mtime, bytes and seat glob are each compared against themselves only as observers of the same path, so the guard is independent of the value the code under test returns.

findings.text: non-blocking: producer_start_decision has no production call site anywhere in the tree at cefafb526 (every reference is inside watch_unit.py itself or its test), so no producer releases its seat and the section's stated release-and-exit behaviour is unreachable until the producer loop calls it; the source manifest records that wiring as a follow-on held out of this node's write scope.

non-blocking: _hosts_match re-implements the short-hostname normalisation the repository already owns in fleet_supervisor._short_hostname (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:270) and already duplicates in paste.py:374, making a third copy; it could shorten the local host through that owner rather than spelling the split again.

non-blocking: the real-record assertion dereferences real_fleet.stat() unconditionally while the before-side reading at line 169 guards with .exists(), so on a host with no fleet record this test errors rather than passing, turning a passing guard into an environment-dependent failure.
